text: Four-day work weeks increase software-team productivity by 39.9 percent in a one-month trial.
Four-day work weeks decrease software-team productivity once output-based measures replace self-reports; apparent 40 percent gains do not survive.
Iceland four-day work week trials maintained service levels and did not increase productivity by 40 percent.
Four-day work weeks increase software-team productivity by 40 percent or more at every company.
UK four-day work week pilot: revenue stayed the same; staff-reported productivity rose but was not independently audited output.
There is no evidence that a universal four-day work week increases software-team productivity after selection effects are removed.
